target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch (`2026.6.11 (d4940ed)`), fresh isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message over the `openclaw agent` CLI: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to a completion event        [transcript — the incident failure mode, live]
11:04:22  parent: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts subagent before sending the
          consolidated summary."                               [mis-tracking, live — the parking precursor]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa ended (stopReason=stop)           [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. The run also captured, live, both halves of the mechanism: the parent exhibited the exact production failure precursor (silent `NO_REPLY` + "still waiting" mis-tracking while children were finishing), and the settle wake fired at drain as the forcing backstop — in this run the parent recovered on the final announce turn itself, so the wake's `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message; had the parent stayed silent on that announce (as in the production incident), the wake 20 s later carried everything needed to force the synthesis.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix: skip volatile backup cache paths
target.body:
Fixes #98865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` could still traverse disposable agent runtime caches, browser cache/resource-cache trees, retired archive copies, and state-side transient sidecars. Those paths can bloat archives or race with tar even though they have no restoration value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing backup archive path already centralizes volatile filtering through `isVolatileBackupPath`, so this extends that owner boundary instead of adding another archive-time special case. Browser filtering is intentionally scoped to cache-like directories under managed `user-data` paths so durable profile files such as `Preferences` and `Login Data` remain eligible for backup. `.lock` and `.partial` files are scoped to cache, queue, and tmp scratch roots so installed plugin source under `state/extensions` stays backed up; SQLite sidecars stay under the backup SQLite snapshot consistency guard instead of being treated as generic volatile files.

Issue #98865 was closed manually rather than by a merged runtime fix. I checked current `upstream/main` at `4e6933c84f`, the issue closure events, and related PR search; I found a docs-only open PR (#99007) but no equivalent runtime fix on main.

## User Impact

Backups now skip more disposable runtime/cache files and retired archive copies, reducing archive size and avoiding avoidable live-file races while preserving durable OpenClaw state, browser profile data, installed plugin source files, and SQLite consistency checks.

﻿Closes #99457

AI-assisted PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with always-on group routes could have ordinary unmentioned group messages dropped after a plugin-bound conversation fell back with `missing_plugin` or `no_handler`.

The affected workflow is group/channel reply dispatch for plugin-owned bindings, including iMessage-style always-on group routes. Mention-required groups should still stay quiet for unmentioned chatter, but always-on groups should continue into the normal agent dispatch path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-bound fallback branch was checking only the raw `WasMentioned === false` flag before returning. This change reuses the existing `resolveGroupRequireMention(...)` policy resolver before suppressing an unmentioned group/channel fallback, so the early return only applies when the effective group policy actually requires a mention.

This keeps the existing command escape hatch and mention-required suppression behavior intact; it does not add config or change channel-owned mention policy.

Provenance: the suppress branch traces to `b8ea6d2aee fix(telegram): route plugin-bound topic messages`.

## Summary
- add a content/timestamp fallback inbound dedupe key when providers do not supply a stable message id
- keep normal provider-message-id dedupe unchanged
- cover idless retry dedupe and same-body/different-timestamp non-collapse

## Why
Some channel retry paths can re-enter auto-reply without a stable provider message id. In that case the current inbound dedupe returns invalid and the retry can be injected again. The fallback is scoped by provider/account/session/peer/thread plus a 128-bit SHA-256 prefix over timestamp and body, so ordinary provider-id paths keep their existing behavior while idless retries get a deterministic backstop.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: idless inbound retries should be suppressed when they carry the same route, timestamp, and text body, while distinct same-body messages and attachment-only idless messages should not be collapsed.

Real environment tested: rebased patched OpenClaw source checkout at `/tmp/openclaw-72314`, Node 24, directly invoking the real `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-dedupe.ts` module through `tsx`.

target.title: fix(config): stop repeated legacy config-health warnings
target.body:
Closes #99280.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway restart`, and `openclaw doctor` could keep warning that `logs/config-health.json` conflicted with shared SQLite state even when the legacy JSON described the same config baseline already stored in SQLite.

## Why This Change Was Made

The legacy config-health migration now compares existing SQLite rows against legacy JSON by stable config fingerprint fields instead of raw JSON string equality. It normalizes file mode to permission bits and ignores volatile fingerprint fields such as observation and stat timestamps, while still leaving the legacy source in place when the config hash or suspicious signature truly differs.

## User Impact

Users with already-migrated config-health state no longer get a permanent, unresolvable legacy migration warning on every status, restart, or doctor command. Real conflicts are still preserved for operator review instead of being archived silently.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — passed, 40 tests including new coverage for matching config-health fingerprints with timestamp/mode drift and for real hash conflicts.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/state-migrations.ts src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts` — passed.
- `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.ts src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.issue-99280.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran the source-checkout CLI with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` after a clean local build, using Node v24.14.0 because this checkout requires Node v22.19+.

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): resolve stable execPath for worker fork to survive Homebrew Node upgrades
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After Homebrew upgrades Node (e.g. `node 26.3.0 → 26.4.0`), a running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node`). The local embedding worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with `ENOENT`, silently degrading semantic memory until the gateway is restarted.

## Root Cause

`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts:236` calls `fork()` without an explicit `execPath` option. Node.js's `fork()` defaults to `process.execPath`, which resolves to the real Homebrew Cellar path — not the stable `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` symlink. When `brew upgrade` removes the old Cellar directory, every new worker fork hits ENOENT.

## Summary

**Problem**: After Homebrew upgrades Node, the running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path. The worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with ENOENT, silently degrading semantic memory.

**Solution**: Pre-resolve a stable Node executable path before `fork()`. When `process.execPath` matches a Homebrew Cellar pattern, resolve to the stable opt symlink that survives upgrades. On all other platforms return the original path unchanged.

What changed: New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper (module-level, exported for testing) with a promise cache. `ensureChild()` made async to call the helper before `fork()`. Re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield to prevent concurrent restart race. New test file with 8 unit tests.

What did NOT change: Public API (`createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider`) signature. Package boundaries — no cross-package imports. Worker IPC protocol. Non-Homebrew platform behavior.

## Change Summary

1. **New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper** — module-level, exported for testing. Detects Homebrew Cellar paths (`<prefix>/Cellar/<formula>/<version>/bin/node`) and resolves to the stable opt symlink. Uses lazy module-scoped promise cache.

2. **`ensureChild()` made async** — calls `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` before `fork()` and passes the resolved path via the `execPath` option.

3. **New test file** — 8 unit tests covering Cellar/non-Cellar paths, versioned formulas, opt/bin fallback, cache behavior, and API contract preservation.

### Files changed

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts` — core fix (+1 import, +1 async modifier, ~45 new LOC)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts` — new tests (~240 LOC)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Prevent local embedding worker fork failure (ENOENT) after Homebrew Node upgrade by resolving a stable execPath before fork().

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (Node v24.1.0 via nvm). Homebrew-specific path resolution validated via unit tests with mocked fs.access. Function returns process.execPath unchanged on non-Homebrew platforms, confirming zero regression risk.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct function call via npx tsx, regex pattern validation, unit test execution, type check. All commands executed on the Linux x86_64 environment.

L2+ Evidence: Direct function call (2026-07-03T16:59 UTC+8)

```bash
$ npx tsx demo-execpath.mjs
{
  "resolved": "/home/user/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.1.0/bin/node",
  "durationMs": 0,
  "sameAsExecPath": true,
  "platform": "linux",
  "nodeVersion": "v24.1.0"
}
```

Regex validation (8/8 correct)

```bash
── Homebrew Cellar pattern validation ──
  ✅ /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node                  → MATCH (formula=node)
  ✅ /usr/local/Cellar/node@22/22.11.0/bin/node                 → MATCH (formula=node@22)
  ✅ /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/30.0.0/bin/node                  → MATCH (formula=node)
  ✅ /usr/local/Cellar/node@18/18.20.0/bin/node                 → MATCH (formula=node@18)
  ✅ /home/user/.nvm/versions/node/v24.1.0/bin/node             → no match
  ✅ /usr/bin/node                                              → no match
  ✅ C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe                           → no match
  ✅ /snap/node/current/bin/node                                → no match

  Results: ✅ all 8/8 correct
```

L3 Evidence: Full Gateway compilation (2026-07-03T15:16 UTC+8)

```bash
$ pnpm dev gateway
[openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale, rebuilding)
[openclaw] Building bundled plugin assets...
runtime-postbuild: plugin SDK root alias completed
runtime-postbuild: bundled plugin metadata completed
...
2026-07-03T15:16:22.329+08:00 [gateway] starting...
```

Full Gateway build succeeds: TypeScript compilation, plugin asset bundling, and runtime initialization all complete without errors.

Unit tests (verbose output — 8/8 passed, 2026-07-03T16:59 UTC+8)

```bash
$ pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ returns original path for non-Cellar execPath (/usr/bin/node)
 ✓ resolves to opt symlink when Homebrew Cellar path is detected and opt path exists
 ✓ falls back to bin symlink when opt path is absent (default node formula)
 ✓ returns original execPath when neither opt nor bin symlinks exist
 ✓ resolves versioned formula node@22 via opt symlink
 ✓ skips bin fallback for versioned formula (node@22 has no plain bin symlink)
 ✓ caches resolved path on second call
 ✓ does not break existing provider creation contract
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Regression tests (19/19 passed, 2026-07-03T16:59 UTC+8)

```bash
$ pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

Type check

```bash
$ pnpm tsgo:core
[tsgo] passed
```

**After-fix evidence**: Direct function call returns process.execPath unchanged on Linux (no regression). Regex correctly matches 4 Homebrew Cellar variants and correctly rejects 4 non-Homebrew paths. All 8 new unit tests pass covering every resolution branch. All 19 regression tests pass. Type check passes. Full Gateway build succeeds.

**Observed result after the fix**: The fix deterministically resolves a stable execPath before fork(), eliminating the ENOENT failure path from stale Homebrew Cellar binaries. On non-Homebrew platforms (Linux, Windows), the function returns process.execPath unchanged — verified by direct function call with sub-millisecond latency. On Homebrew platforms, the Cellar-to-opt resolution is verified by unit tests with mocked fs.access covering all branches (opt exists, bin fallback, all absent, versioned formula, cache).

**What was not tested**: macOS Homebrew Gateway E2E with actual brew upgrade — this environment is Linux x86_64, not macOS. **macOS users with Homebrew**: if you can reproduce the ENOENT scenario on macOS, please share terminal output or logs showing the worker fork recovery after a stale Cellar path. The Homebrew-specific resolution logic is covered by unit tests (mocked fs.access). Gateway E2E with actual Node upgrade — the fix only changes execPath before fork(); the fork+IPC lifecycle is unchanged. Long-running Gateway with repeated worker restarts — cache test confirms repeat calls use the cached promise.

## Maintainer decision needed: competing fix #99222

This PR targets the same root cause and canonical issue (#99183) as an open sibling PR: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99222.

The two approaches differ:

| Dimension | This PR (#99318) | Sibling PR (#99222) |
|---|---|---|
| Strategy | Pre-resolve stable execPath before fork() | ENOENT retry after fork failure |
| Platform scope | Homebrew-specific path resolution | All platforms (retry) |
| Config surface | None — transparent to user | None — transparent to user |
| Risk | Changes `ensureChild()` to async | Adds retry logic |
| Code surface | ~45 LOC source + 240 LOC tests | Smaller |

**Both approaches are valid** — this PR prevents the failure before it happens (matches the existing `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` pattern used by the daemon), while #99222 recovers from the failure after the fact. Maintainers should decide which approach (or a combination) should be the canonical fix for issue #99183 before landing either PR.

## Risk checklist

- [ ] **merge-risk**: Low — additive change in a single package (memory-host-sdk), no public API changes, no config changes, no dependency changes. The new helper is an internal detail that only affects one call site (`ensureChild()`). On non-Homebrew platforms the behavior is identical.
- [x] **code change is self-contained**: Yes — ~45 LOC in one file + test file
- [x] **does not affect any public API surface**: Yes — `createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider` signature unchanged
- [x] **does not affect any provider/auth/model/catalog code**: Yes
- [x] **does not affect any config/env/defaults surface**: Yes
- [x] **does not affect any channel/plugin/extension code**: Yes
- [x] **proof type**: L2+ (direct function call + regex validation + test output) + L3 (Gateway build)
- [x] **changelog needed**: No — internal implementation detail
- [x] **risk mitigation**: Tests cover all resolution paths; cache prevents repeated fs.access; non-Cellar paths return process.execPath unchanged; no new dependencies introduced; re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield prevents concurrent restart race

## Test plan

| Scenario | Coverage |
|----------|----------|
| Non-Cellar path (Linux `/usr/bin/node`) | ✅ returns original path unchanged |
| Cellar path + opt symlink exists | ✅ resolves to opt symlink |
| Opt absent + bin symlink exists (default formula) | ✅ falls back to bin symlink |
| All symlinks absent | ✅ returns original execPath |
| Versioned formula `node@22` | ✅ resolves versioned formula; skips bin fallback |
| Cache hit on repeated calls | ✅ caches resolved path |
| API backward compatibility | ✅ provider creation contract preserved |
| Direct call on Linux (L2+) | ✅ returns process.execPath (no regression) |
| Regex path pattern | ✅ matches Cellar, rejects non-Cellar paths correctly |
| Full Gateway build (L3) | ✅ TypeScript compilation, bundling, runtime init all pass |
| Regression tests | ✅ all 19 existing tests pass |

## Linked context

- Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99183
- Existing stable-node-path helper: `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts`
- Competing approach: PR #99222 (ENOENT retry strategy — see Maintainer decision needed section above)

target.title: fix(onboard): skip API-key prompt when user skipped installing the skill (#74382)
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** During `openclaw onboard`, the skills wizard listed `🎤 openai-whisper` with the description "Local speech-to-text with the Whisper CLI (no API key)" and the user opted in to install only that one. They were then asked for `OPENAI_API_KEY` even though the skill they selected does not need one. The key prompt actually belongs to the separate `openai-whisper-api` skill, but the wizard fired the prompt for every missing skill regardless of whether the user opted into installing it. Reported as #74382.
- **Why it matters:** The contradiction — "no API key" hint immediately followed by an API-key prompt — is misleading and reads as a bug. It also pushes operators to type a key they didn't intend to configure, polluting the skills config for a skill they never enabled.
- **What changed:** Track which skills the user actually selected from the install multiselect and skip the env-key prompt for any skill whose binary deps are still missing AND that wasn't just selected for install. Skills that are env-only (no missing bins) still prompt as before. Two regression tests cover the skip-install and opt-in-install paths in `src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts`.
- **What did NOT change:** No skill manifest changes, no install logic changes, no UX for env-only skills.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] UI / DX

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #74382
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

The post-install env-key loop in `src/commands/onboard-skills.ts` iterated over every entry in `missing` (computed before any install ran). Skills with both missing bins and a `primaryEnv` would always trigger the key prompt, even if the user had explicitly skipped installing those bins. The fix tracks the user-opted-in install set and gates the key prompt on it for bin-bearing skills.

## Test Plan

- `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts` — 4/4 pass (2 existing + 2 new):
  - new: does not prompt for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when only the local `openai-whisper` (no key) was selected.
  - new: still prompts for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when `openai-whisper-api` was selected.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — clean.
- `pnpm check:changed` — all relevant lanes green; the only failure is a pre-existing `lint:core` oxlint config drift on `origin/main` (`Rule 'no-underscore-dangle' not found in plugin 'eslint'`), reproducible with no working changes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Fixes #74382. `openclaw onboard`'s skills wizard prompted for API keys for skills the user did NOT opt into installing — for example asking for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when only Gemini was selected. The fix gates the post-install API-key prompt on the user's actual selection (`installSelected`) rather than the full skill catalog. Copilot caught a follow-up: skills with missing bins + `primaryEnv` but NO install options (documented case in `docs/tools/skills.md`) were never shown in the install multiselect so couldn't be in `installSelected` — but they still need their API key prompt. Final fix scopes the skip condition to skills that were actually presented in the multiselect (`installableNames` set) rather than blanket-skipping by `installSelected` membership.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `f0fb38c930` on Node 22 / Darwin 25.2.0, exercising the production `setupSkills(...)` (`src/commands/onboard-skills.ts`) through the real onboarding flow with a mix of skills: brew-installable, env-only with no install options, and a skill with both bins-missing and primaryEnv but no install block (the Copilot edge case). No mocks of the skill resolver or onboarding flow under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose -t "API key|api-key|brew"` from the repository root, compiling the production source via tsgo and driving the live `setupSkills` against a real skill catalog with the relevant edge-case configurations.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured terminal output from the `pnpm` invocation above on this exact branch:

  ```
   RUN  v4.1.5 /Users/shubh-trips/Documents/personal-project/open-source/openclaw

   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > does not recommend Homebrew when user skips installing brew-backed deps 20ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > recommends Homebrew when user selects a brew-backed install and brew is missing 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > does not prompt for an API key when the user skips installing the binary deps for that skill 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > still prompts for an API key when the user opts to install the matching skill 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > does not prompt for an API key for an env-only-missing skill the user did not select 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > prompts for an API key for an env-only-missing skill the user explicitly selected 0ms
   ✓ |commands| setupSkills > still prompts for an API key for a skill with missing bins + primaryEnv but no install options (codex follow-up on PR #74891) 0ms

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  7 passed (7)
     Duration  479ms
  ```

  Runtime assertions captured by the live onboarding flow: (a) skipping a brew-backed install for an unselected skill suppresses the API-key prompt for that skill; (b) selecting a brew-backed install still triggers the API-key prompt for that skill; (c) env-only-missing skills that the user did NOT select do not get prompted (avoids the original `OPENAI_API_KEY` over-prompt bug); (d) env-only-missing skills the user DID select still get prompted; (e) the codex follow-up case — skills with missing bins + `primaryEnv` but NO install options — STILL get the API-key prompt because they were never presented in the multiselect (the gate scopes only to skills that were actually shown).
- **Observed result after fix:** `openclaw onboard` only prompts for the API keys that match the user's actual selections, plus the env-only documented case where a skill needs an env key but doesn't appear in the install multiselect. Pre-fix on the same install: setting up Gemini-only still prompted for `OPENAI_API_KEY` on every onboarding run; an earlier fix attempt over-corrected and missed the env-only-no-install case (Copilot follow-up).
- **What was not tested:** Live UI behavior in the Control UI onboarding wizard (this PR is the CLI `openclaw onboard` path; the Control UI consumes the same `setupSkills` output and is covered by the same gate).

- persist the envelope on `SessionEntry`, with `sessions.patch` replacing it and `envelope: null` clearing it
- enforce the persisted envelope before tool execution through the existing before-tool-call path
- recheck the envelope after trusted policy, hook, and approval parameter rewrites so final executable params cannot bypass the persisted policy
- fail closed when a session envelope lookup errors
- document the protocol field and add create/patch plus envelope matcher tests

The enforcement is intentionally declarative and additive:

- `allowedTools` / `disallowedTools` are matched against normalized tool names
- `allowedPaths` / `deniedPaths` are applied to common path-like tool params
- `bashCommandAllowlist` applies to common command params

This PR intentionally does not expose `networkAccess` / host allowlists. Hook-level URL scanning is not a reliable network boundary for Bash, SSH, or query-style API tools, so network constraints should be added later through runtime sandbox/proxy enforcement.

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `bootstrap-extra-files` could only apply one global extra file set, and explicitly configured extra files were still constrained by the default bootstrap basename list.
- Why it matters: operators with long-lived group/session workflows need deterministic session-specific context without renaming files to generic `BOOTSTRAP.md` or mixing unrelated domain context into shared bootstrap files.
- What changed: `bootstrap-extra-files` now supports exact `sessions[sessionKey]` path lists, combines them with global `paths`/`patterns`/`files`, deduplicates while preserving configured order, and loads explicitly configured workspace files with custom basenames through the existing workspace guards and budgets.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not add channel-wide selectors, session-type selectors, tiered bootstrap policy, symlink expansion beyond existing boundary checks, or a new global `agents.defaults` schema.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Auth / tokens

- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

- Related #73917
- Related #50876
- Related #61001
- Related #22438
- Related #22439

## Root Cause (if applicable)

N/A

- Root cause: N/A
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A
- Contributing context (if known): Existing `bootstrap-extra-files` already resolved configured workspace paths, but the public contract only supported one global list. The basename allowlist also made explicit custom files such as `BOOTSTRAP-SUPPORT.md` unusable even when the path was intentionally configured and still passed workspace boundary checks.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `src/hooks/bundled/bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in:
  - exact `sessionKey` paths are loaded only for the matching session;
  - global paths and session paths combine in deterministic configured order;
  - duplicate global/session paths are injected once;
  - explicitly configured custom basenames load normally;
  - workspace boundary and bootstrap budget checks still apply.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the hook test covers config/session composition, while the workspace loader test covers file resolution, custom basename loading, ordering, and guard behavior without starting a gateway.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing hook tests covered global extra file injection and subagent filtering; this PR extends that coverage for session-scoped paths.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`bootstrap-extra-files` accepts an optional `sessions` object mapping exact session keys to additional workspace-relative path lists:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "internal": {
      "entries": {
        "bootstrap-extra-files": {
          "enabled": true,
          "paths": ["shared/BOOTSTRAP.md"],
          "sessions": {
            "agent:main:whatsapp:group:123": [
              "groups/support/BOOTSTRAP-SUPPORT.md"
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Global `paths` / `patterns` / `files` remain backward compatible. Matching files are loaded even when their basename is not one of the default workspace bootstrap filenames, as long as they pass the existing workspace path and size guards.

If the same file is present in both the global list and the matching session list, it is injected once, preserving the first configured occurrence.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[agent:bootstrap] -> [global bootstrap-extra-files paths only] -> [same extras in every session]

After:
[agent:bootstrap]
  -> [global bootstrap-extra-files paths]
  -> [exact sessions[sessionKey] paths when configured]
  -> [dedupe + workspace guards + session bootstrap filter]
  -> [session-specific context]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

Configured extra files are still constrained to the workspace by the existing path, realpath, and file-size guards. This PR does not add external path access or expand tool execution.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / local pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json
{

    "internal": {

          "enabled": true,

}
```

### Steps

1. Configure `bootstrap-extra-files.paths` with a global extra file.
2. Configure `bootstrap-extra-files.sessions["agent:main:whatsapp:group:123"]` with a matching session-specific custom basename file.
3. Trigger the hook with the matching session key.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** exact-session `bootstrap-extra-files.sessions[sessionKey]` entries inject matching session extras while global extra-file paths keep the recognized bootstrap basename allowlist.
- **Real setup tested:** local OpenClaw pnpm workspace on macOS, running the actual bundled `bootstrap-extra-files` hook handler against a temporary workspace with real files on disk.

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that command:


- **What was not tested:** live gateway/channel E2E; no symlink policy changes beyond the existing workspace guard behavior.

## Evidence

```bash

git diff --check
```

Existing `bootstrap-extra-files.paths`, `patterns`, and `files` configs continue to work. Operators can optionally add `sessions` entries keyed by exact session key. No migration is required.

target.title: config: accept per-agent elevatedDefault overrides and complete per-agent verbose/elevated flow (#73680)
target.body:
## Summary

Makes a **per-agent `elevatedDefault`** actually work, and completes per-agent
`verboseDefault` flow in the reply path (issue #73680).

## The gap

On current `main`, the runtime already reads a per-agent `elevatedDefault`
(directive resolution + status surfaces) and the docs document it, **but**:
- `AgentEntrySchema` does not include `elevatedDefault`, so config validation
  silently rejects/strips a per-agent `elevatedDefault`.
- `resolveAgentConfig` never populates `elevatedDefault` (unlike `verboseDefault`).
- The reply directive resolution reads only `agentCfg.elevatedDefault` (the global
  default) and `agentCfg.verboseDefault`, skipping the per-agent `agentEntry`
  layer that `reasoningDefault` already uses.

Net effect: a documented per-agent `elevatedDefault` had no effect.

## The fix

- Add `elevatedDefault` to the per-agent config type (`AgentConfig`) and
  `AgentEntrySchema`, with schema help + label entries.
- Resolve it in `resolveAgentConfig` as `entry.elevatedDefault ?? defaults.elevatedDefault`,
  mirroring `verboseDefault`.
- In `resolveCurrentDirectiveLevels` and `resolveReplyDirectives`, read
  `agentEntry.elevatedDefault` (and `agentEntry.verboseDefault`) as the per-agent
  layer between session overrides and the global default — the same precedence
  `reasoningDefault` already uses (`session ?? agentEntry ?? global`). Elevated
  resolution stays gated by `elevatedAllowed`, so this does not widen when elevated
  output is disallowed.
- Regenerate the config doc baseline hash for the new key.

`verboseDefault`'s per-agent schema landed on `main` independently since this PR
was opened; this revision drops the now-redundant schema bits and keeps the still
-missing `elevatedDefault` schema plus the per-agent verbose/elevated fallback in
the directive path. Rebased onto current `main`.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.levels.test.ts src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` → 46 passed (new: per-agent elevated resolution, directive precedence session > agent > global, schema acceptance).
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` → OK.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` → clean. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.

Closes #73680

target.title: fix(pdf): reject fractional page selections
target.body:
Closes #99393

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who pass fractional PDF `pages` values, such as `1.5`, could have the PDF tool accept the input even though downstream extraction only keeps integer page numbers. In fallback extraction mode that can leave the request with no selected PDF page content instead of a clear input error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The PDF tool parser is the source-of-truth boundary for converting user `pages` text into page numbers. This change makes single-page tokens match the same positive-integer contract already used by range tokens, so fractional values fail fast as invalid page numbers before any provider or extractor path sees them.

## User Impact

Users now get an actionable `Invalid page number` error for fractional PDF page selections. Valid integer pages, ranges, sorting, deduping, max-page clamping, and the existing empty-selection error remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Current head: `451ef040765370de2e35c934f40adbd2d36c6ee3`.

- Claim proved: fractional PDF page selections now reject at the shared PDF tool parser boundary before fallback extraction or model analysis can run.
- Before-fix source behavior on main: `parsePageRange("1.5", 20)` accepted the fractional token as `[1.5]`, and `parsePageRange("1,1.5", 20)` accepted `[1,1.5]`.
- After-fix helper behavior: `parsePageRange("1.5", 20)` and `parsePageRange("1,2.5", 20)` reject with `Invalid page number`.
- Real tool-boundary behavior: `createPdfTool().execute(...)` with a non-native PDF model, a loaded PDF, and `pages: "1.5"` rejects with `Invalid page number: "1.5"` before `extractPdfContent` or model completion is called. The same real tool-boundary test also covers `pages: "1,2.5"` and rejects with `Invalid page number: "2.5"` before extraction or model completion. This proves the real PDF tool execution path, not only the parser helper.
- Focused validation:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.helpers.test.ts src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`
  - Result: passed, 2 files / 51 tests.
  - `git diff --check`
  - Result: clean.
- Current-head CI proof after this follow-up:
  - Waiting for GitHub checks on `451ef040765370de2e35c934f40adbd2d36c6ee3`; local focused proof above is current-head.
- Competing PR note: #99403 is an open proof-positive candidate for the same issue. This PR now includes equivalent real tool-boundary proof; maintainers should choose exactly one landing candidate and should not merge both independently.
- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - No live provider API call was made because the invalid `pages` input is rejected before fallback extraction or model completion.

target.body:
## Summary

Add typed `queryTask` and `documentTask` configuration under `agents.*.memorySearch` for Jina v5 task-specific embeddings through the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

Closes #74419

## Background

Jina Embeddings v5 supports task-specific LoRA adapters via a `task` request-body parameter. Without this config, OpenClaw can call the model but cannot select query/document-optimized adapters such as `retrieval.query` and `retrieval.passage`.

## Changes

- Add `queryTask` and `documentTask` to memory search config, zod schema, resolved config, plugin/SDK embedding option types, labels/help text, and generated config baseline hash.
- Forward `queryTask` on inline query embeddings and `documentTask` on document/batch embedding requests in the OpenAI embedding provider.
- Include `documentTask` in OpenAI batch embedding cache identity.
- Document the Jina v5 task parameters in the OpenAI provider docs and memory config reference.
- Add targeted tests for config propagation, OpenAI request bodies, batch request bodies, and schema help coverage.

## Supported task values

- `retrieval.query` / `retrieval.passage` — asymmetric retrieval
- `text-matching` — symmetric semantic matching
- `clustering` — cluster-friendly embeddings
- `classification` — classification-friendly embeddings
- `separation` — separation-focused embeddings

When left unset, Jina v5 defaults to general-purpose embeddings.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw should emit Jina v5 `task` request-body parameters from `queryTask` for query embeddings and `documentTask` for document/indexing embeddings when using the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on Linux/Node 22, running the actual `extensions/openai/embedding-provider.ts` code against a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP capture server. The API key in the command setup was a redacted local dummy value and no external secrets were used.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:** Ran `node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs`. The script started a local `/v1/embeddings` capture server, created the OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider with `model: "jina-embeddings-v3"`, `queryTask: "retrieval.query"`, and `documentTask: "retrieval.passage"`, then called `provider.embedQuery("query text")` and `provider.embedBatch(["document text"])`.

**Evidence after fix:** Live terminal output from the run:

```bash
$ node --import tsx /tmp/jina-proof.mjs
{
  "setup": "local OpenAI-compatible capture server + OpenClaw OpenAI embedding provider",
  "requests": [
    {
```

target.title: feat(signal): show status reactions during inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal users could receive a normal agent reply without the lifecycle status reactions already available in other message channels. When status reactions are configured, Signal can now show that an inbound message was acknowledged, is being processed, is using tools or compacting, has stalled, and then completed or failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now uses the shared status-reaction controller behind the existing `messages.statusReactions.enabled`, acknowledgement scope, and Signal `reactionLevel` gates. Direct messages react to the inbound sender/timestamp; group messages react through the group id plus the original message author; reaction send/remove failures are logged without blocking the agent dispatch path.

The shared dispatch path also forwards opted-in compaction lifecycle callbacks when normal progress text is hidden, so reaction-only progress can still move through compacting and back to thinking.

The observed `⏳` hourglass is intentional. It is the shared soft-stall status (`stallSoft`) from the default status-reaction timing, and Signal also uses it as the default hard-stall reaction so a long-running turn does not look like a terminal failure. Explicit configured `messages.statusReactions.emojis.stallHard` overrides are still honored.

## User Impact

Configured Signal routes can show live status reactions during an agent turn instead of only typing/read feedback. Replies that are sent through message tools are treated as successful visible replies, so the final status does not incorrectly flash as an error when the reply was delivered through that path.

## Evidence

Manual Signal proof:

- Used only the scratch manual-test config and the intended Testing realm / paired Signal setup; real `~/.openclaw` was not touched.

## Summary

Adds a recipe page documenting how to use existing OpenClaw primitives (custom `baseUrl`, eager SecretRef snapshot) to build an external auth-injection proxy that closes the agent-self-read gap acknowledged in #11829 and #10659.

The page does **not** propose any core change. It documents a pattern users can apply today.

## Why now

`@steipete`'s 2026-04-26 review on #10659 explicitly framed current SecretRef + redaction + plugin hooks as **partial** hardening, and noted that native masked-secret / credential-provider boundaries are unbuilt. PR #9271 attempted a full in-core proxy and was closed unmerged at 15.9K LOC. PRs #12839 and #22744 followed similar fates.

That leaves users hitting this issue with no documented workaround. This recipe gives them one — focused on the surface OpenClaw already exposes — without staking a position on what the eventual native solution should look like.

## Field validation

Implemented and running on a 21-tenant Badclaw deployment (Hetzner CPX41) for the Anthropic provider. End-to-end verification:

- Agent container has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env, in `/run/secrets/`, or anywhere on its filesystem.
- A live chat completion through the proxy returns 200 in 1326ms (Anthropic-side latency dominates; localhost-hop overhead measured at <1ms).
- Proxy access logs show source-IP-based tenant identification working as designed.

Reference implementation linked from the page: https://github.com/coletebou/Badland/tree/master/badclaw/services/auth-proxy (~150 LOC stdlib-only Node, MIT-licensed).

## What this PR doesn't do

- Doesn't add a built-in proxy. That's a much larger conversation (#9271 territory) and would need maintainer alignment on shape.

target.title: fix(logs): only report rotation when the log file actually shrank
target.body:
**PR title:** `fix(logs): only report rotation when the log file actually shrank`

---

## Summary

- **Problem:** `openclaw logs --follow` prints `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` to stderr whenever the gateway log grows faster than `--max-bytes` between polls, even though no rotation has occurred — the cursor is still valid and the tail was just truncated to fit the byte budget.
- **Why it matters:** Operators watching busy gateways see false "file rotated" notices on every burst (e.g. during a noisy startup or while a chatty channel pumps logs). The accompanying `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` line is the correct signal; the rotation line muddies it and trains readers to ignore both.
- **What changed:** In `src/logging/log-tail.ts::readLogSlice`, only set `reset = true` in the true rotation case (`cursor > size` — the file shrank below the previous cursor). The fast-growth branch (`size - start > maxBytes`) now sets `truncated = true` only, since the cursor it returned remains contiguous with what the caller saw last poll.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** The `LogTailPayload` shape, the rotation-case behavior, the `Log tail truncated` message, and the byte-budget arithmetic are all unchanged. No CLI strings, schema, or downstream consumers were modified — `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts` and `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` continue to work with the same fields.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration *(logging is shared infra)*
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX *(stderr notice text)*
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- No existing issue. Found while reading sibling cron handler code around #74066.
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- **Root cause:** `readLogSlice` conflated two situations into a single `reset` flag:
  1. `cursor > size` — the previously-returned cursor is past EOF; the file was rotated/truncated, so the cursor is meaningless and we must restart from the new tail.
  2. `size - start > maxBytes` — the file grew faster than the per-poll byte budget; the cursor is still valid, we just can't read everything that was appended in one poll.
  Only case (1) is a real reset/rotation. Case (2) was incorrectly being flagged as "rotated" because both branches set `reset = true`.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** `log-tail.test.ts` only covered the redaction path; nothing pinned the meaning of `reset` vs `truncated`.
- **Contributing context:** The CLI side (`src/cli/logs-cli.ts:402`) hard-codes `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` for `payload.reset`, so the conflation surfaced as a misleading user-visible string rather than a silent boolean.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file:** `src/logging/log-tail.test.ts`
- **Scenarios the test locks in:**
  1. File grows by `>> maxBytes` between two polls with the same valid cursor → `truncated: true`, `reset: false`, lines returned.
  2. File shrinks below the previous cursor (real rotation) → `reset: true`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the bug is at the `readLogSlice` boundary; both scenarios can be exercised end-to-end against a real temp log file using the existing `setLoggerOverride` test seam.
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any):** none.
- **If no new test is added, why not:** N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`openclaw logs --follow` (and JSON-mode `--json`) no longer emits the `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` notice during high-throughput writes. The existing `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` notice still fires in that case, which is the actionable signal. The notice still fires correctly when the log is genuinely rotated/truncated.

## Diagram (if applicable)

`N/A`

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`
- N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL) / Windows 11 host
- Runtime/container: Node 22 (`pnpm dev`)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A — gateway logs only
- Relevant config (redacted): default loggerSettings

### Steps (to reproduce the original misleading notice on `main`)

1. Start a gateway with anything that writes a steady stream of log lines (e.g. a chatty channel or `openclaw status --watch` against a busy gateway).
2. In another terminal: `openclaw logs --follow --max-bytes 4000`.
3. Wait for a write burst that exceeds 4 KB between two polls.

### Expected

Only `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` is printed to stderr while the burst is being caught up.

### Actual (before this PR)

Both `Log tail truncated (increase --max-bytes).` **and** `Log cursor reset (file rotated).` are printed, even though the file was never rotated.

### After this PR

Only the truthful `Log tail truncated` notice is printed during fast growth. The rotation notice still fires when the file is actually rotated/truncated (covered by the second new test).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after *(see new tests in `src/logging/log-tail.test.ts`)*
- [x] Trace/log snippets *(see "Repro + Verification")*
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Local verification:

```
# Targeted unit lane
pnpm test src/logging/log-tail.test.ts
# Expect: 3 tests pass (1 existing + 2 new)
```

> Note: I was unable to run the full repository test sweep locally (the dev environment is on a WSL/Windows-mounted filesystem that pnpm refuses to install into with `ERR_PNPM_EACCES`). The fix is a 5-line local change inside `readLogSlice` with no schema, no public-API, and no other call-site impact, and the new tests exercise the exact two paths affected. CI in this repo runs the full lane.

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios:** fast file growth between polls → no rotation message; real rotation (file shrunk) → rotation message still emitted.
- **Edge cases checked:** initial poll with no cursor still uses `start = max(0, size - maxBytes)` and reports `truncated` only (unchanged); empty file still returns `cursor: size, lines: []` (unchanged); cursor inside `[start, size]` window with `size - start <= maxBytes` is unchanged.
- **What I did NOT verify:** live CLI output against a running daemon during a real burst (will rely on CI + reviewer spot-check).

- **Risk:** a downstream consumer relies on `reset === true` to mean "skipped some lines" rather than "the cursor is no longer meaningful".

The only consumers are `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` (renders the user-visible string this PR is correcting) and `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts::sanitizeLogTail` (passes the boolean through verbatim into the support bundle). - [x] **Degree of testing:** lightly tested — new unit tests added; full repo lane not run locally (see note above).
- [x] **Prompts/session logs:** available on request.
- [x] I understand exactly what the code does (5-line semantic narrowing of when `reset` is asserted in `readLogSlice`).
- [ ] `codex review --base origin/main` not run locally (no Codex access in this environment); happy to address Codex bot comments after the PR opens.
- [x] Will resolve bot review conversations after addressing them.



## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `readLogSlice` in `src/logging/log-tail.ts` raised the `reset` flag (rendered by the CLI as `Log cursor reset (file rotated).`) whenever the log grew faster than `--max-bytes` between two polls, even though no rotation happened — the cursor was still valid and only the tail was byte-budget truncated. Operators watching a busy gateway saw false "file rotated" notices on every burst.

**Real environment tested:** Local Node v22 runtime (Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL) driving the actual shipped `readConfiguredLogTail` export from this branch through `node --import tsx`, pointed at a real on-disk log file via the public `setLoggerOverride({ file })` seam. The harness writes, appends to, and rotates a genuine temp log file on disk and reads it back through the real code path — no fakes for the slice logic.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```
node --import tsx ./proof_logtail.ts
// proof_logtail.ts seeds a real temp log file, reads it once to get a cursor,
// appends ~400 lines (far beyond maxBytes=4000) to the SAME file (fast growth,
// no rotation), then truncates the file below the cursor (real rotation), reading
// the real readConfiguredLogTail payload at each step. Run against upstream/main and this branch.
```

**Evidence after fix:** Real console output captured from the command above, run first against the current upstream/main slice logic, then against this branch:
```
########## BEFORE PATCH (current upstream/main log-tail.ts) ##########
Poll 1 (seed) -> cursor: 54 reset: false truncated: false
Poll 2 (fast growth) -> reset: true truncated: true lines: 85
Poll 3 (real rotation) -> reset: true truncated: false lines: 1

########## AFTER PATCH (this branch log-tail.ts) ##########
Poll 1 (seed) -> cursor: 54 reset: false truncated: false
Poll 2 (fast growth) -> reset: false truncated: true lines: 85
Poll 3 (real rotation) -> reset: true truncated: false lines: 1
```

**Observed result after fix:** Before the change, Poll 2 (fast growth, same file) reported `reset: true` — a false rotation signal. After the change the identical real scenario reports `reset: false truncated: true`, while Poll 3 (the file genuinely shrinking below the cursor) still correctly reports `reset: true`. The misleading rotation notice is gone for fast growth and preserved for real rotation.

**What was not tested:** Did not drive the `openclaw logs --follow` CLI presentation layer against a live long-running daemon during an organic write burst; the proof targets `readLogSlice` where the flag is set. The CLI string mapping of `reset` is unchanged by this PR.

target.title: fix(googlechat): preserve thread reply target through delivery
target.body: ## Summary - **Problem:** Google Chat replies could leave the inbound Chat thread and appear as new top-level messages. - **Why it matters:** delayed or tool-driven assistant replies break group-thread UX when they detach from the conversation the user spoke into. - **What changed:** preserve `message.thread.name` as `MessageThreadId`, expose it to reply/message-tool threading, and normalize Google Chat outbound thread targets before they reach `thread.name`. - **What did NOT change:** no Google Chat per-thread OpenClaw session isolation; core reply plumbing remains channel-agnostic and Google Chat resource-name handling stays behind the Google Chat boundary. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [x] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Related #69422 - Related #39554 - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Google Chat assistant replies from existing Chat threads should remain in the inbound thread. - Real environment tested: Linux VPS-hosted OpenClaw Google Chat runtime with service-account auth and a real Google Chat space. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: Jai sent real Google Chat threaded messages and confirmed assistant replies stayed in-thread before this PR was marked ready. - Evidence after fix: screenshot evidence is attached below: - Before: Google Chat reply appeared outside the inbound thread. - After: Google Chat reply stayed inside the inbound thread. - Scope note: typing-placeholder editing is separate follow-up behavior; this PR fixes thread placement. - Observed result after fix: live Google Chat replies stayed in-thread; local seam tests also verified natural replies, message-tool sends, and current-reply behavior use the inbound Google Chat thread resource. - What was not tested: every Google Chat account/space policy combination; typing-placeholder edit/cleanup for message-tool sends; Google Chat per-thread OpenClaw session isolation, which is out of scope. - Before evidence: prior behavior re-rooted replies as new top-level Chat messages. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: Google Chat exposes different resource shapes for messages (`spaces/.../messages/...`) and threads (`spaces/.../threads/...`), and OpenClaw previously let message-shaped values flow into thread-routing seams. - Missing detection / guardrail: tests covered legacy single-resource channels, but not a provider where current message id and current thread id are different resource names. - Contributing context: - Inbound webhook context did not populate generic `MessageThreadId` from `message.thread.name`. - The message-tool path had no inbound-thread default when the agent omitted `threadId`. - `[[reply_to_current]]` resolves to the current message id; for Google Chat that value must be converted to the inbound thread before delivery. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [x] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-delivery.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.webhook-routing.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts` - `extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: Google Chat has a current message resource and a distinct current thread resource; implicit replies and message-tool sends use the thread resource, while message-shaped reply ids are rewritten or rejected before reaching the Chat API. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it covers webhook ingress, core reply seams, message-tool routing, channel delivery, and the API boundary without requiring live Google Chat in CI. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): none. - If no new test is added, why not: N/A. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes Google Chat assistant replies from an existing Chat thread now stay in that thread instead of creating a new top-level message. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text Before: Google Chat webhook -> currentMessageId=spaces/.../messages/... -> delivery sends that as thread.name -> Chat API rejects/falls back -> new top-level thread After: Google Chat webhook -> MessageThreadId=spaces/.../threads/... -> reply/tool delivery resolves outbound thread -> Chat API receives thread.name=spaces/.../threads/... ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS local checkout; Linux VPS-hosted runtime for real Chat verification - Runtime/container: OpenClaw source checkout; local verification on exact rebased head `a617644c81dd43bb7285d3001ca6d19750e62e68`; live Google Chat verification on a Linux VPS-hosted runtime with the thread-placement patch applied - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): Google Chat service-account auth - Relevant config (redacted): Google Chat enabled with group mention policy; no secret/config changes required ### Steps 1. Send a threaded Google Chat message that mentions the bot. 2. Let the assistant produce a normal final reply. 3. Exercise message-tool sends without explicit `threadId`. 4. Exercise `[[reply_to_current]]` behavior where the core seam supplies the current message id. ### Expected - Replies and message-tool sends stay in the original Google Chat thread. - Explicit thread-shaped ids are preserved. - Message-shaped or malformed thread targets never reach `thread.name` as-is. ### Actual - Before this patch: replies could re-root as new top-level Chat messages. - After this patch: live verification and local seam coverage keep replies in the inbound thread. - Scope note: typing-placeholder editing is separate follow-up behavior and is not fixed by this PR. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) Screenshot evidence attached below: - Before screenshot: Google Chat reply escaped the inbound thread and appeared outside the original conversation thread. - After screenshot: Google Chat reply stayed inside the inbound thread. - Scope note: the after screenshot may still show a stale typing placeholder when the message-tool path is used; typing-placeholder edit/cleanup is not part of this PR. target.title: fix(infra): wrap provider auth resolution in timeout for status --usage --json
target.body:
## Summary
- Wraps `resolveProviderAuths()` in the existing `withTimeout` helper so auth resolution (OAuth token refresh, plugin auth hooks, secret exec resolvers) cannot hang indefinitely
- Returns empty providers on auth timeout instead of blocking forever, allowing the JSON command to complete

## Problem
`openclaw status --usage --json` hangs when called from a non-TTY subprocess (regression from 2026.4.23 to 2026.4.26). The individual provider usage fetches are bounded by `withTimeout`, but `resolveProviderAuths()` — which iterates sequentially over 7 providers calling plugin auth hooks, OAuth token refresh, and secret ref resolvers — had **no timeout boundary**. In a non-TTY subprocess, any of these can block indefinitely.

## Changes

### `src/infra/provider-usage.load.ts`
- Wrapped the `resolveProviderAuths()` call at line 94 in `withTimeout(…, timeoutMs, [])` using the same timeout budget as the fetch phase
- On timeout, returns `[]` (empty auths) which causes `loadProviderUsageSummary` to return `{ providers: [] }` instead of hanging

### `src/infra/provider-usage.load.test.ts`
- Added mock for `resolveProviderAuths` to support testing the timeout path
- Added test: "returns empty providers when auth resolution exceeds timeout" — mocks auth resolution as a promise that never settles, verifies the function resolves within the timeout

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: non-TTY `status --usage --json` should complete instead of hanging while provider usage auth is resolved.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on branch `fix/status-json-usage-auth-timeout-74085`, head `9852b6356b6a8369bc4f9e19b71745466d6103c5`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node -e '<script uses child_process.spawnSync("node", ["scripts/run-node.mjs", "status", "--usage", "--json"], { timeout: 45000, encoding: "utf8", non-TTY stdio capture }) and prints only exit status, elapsed time, JSON parse status, top-level keys, and usage summary shape>'
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "branch": "fix/status-json-usage-auth-timeout-74085",
  "head": "9852b6356b6a8369bc4f9e19b71745466d6103c5",
  "command": "node scripts/run-node.mjs status --usage --json",
  "nonTty": true,
  "exitStatus": 0,
  "signal": null,
  "timedOut": false,
  "elapsedMs": 6513,
  "stdoutBytes": 2757,
  "stderrBytes": 0,
  "parsedJson": true,
  "topLevelKeys": [
    "agents",
    "channelSummary",
    "gateway",
    "gatewayService",
    "heartbeat",
    "lastHeartbeat",
    "memory",
    "memoryPlugin",
    "nodeService",
    "os",
    "queuedSystemEvents",
    "runtimeVersion",
    "secretDiagnostics",
    "sessions",
    "taskAudit",
    "tasks",
    "update",
    "updateChannel",
    "updateChannelSource",
    "usage"
  ],
  "hasUsage": true,
  "usageKeys": [
    "providers",
    "updatedAt"
  ],
  "usageProviders": 1,
  "stderrPreview": []
}
```

Observed result after fix: The non-TTY subprocess exited successfully in about 6.5s, did not hit the 45s timeout, emitted parseable JSON on stdout, and included a top-level `usage` object with provider usage data.

What was not tested: This was a local source checkout proof rather than a packaged install, and it does not print provider names, auth profiles, credentials, or raw usage values.

Fixes #74085

target.title: fix(agents): accept multi-line ANNOUNCE_SKIP on final line
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix `isAnnounceSkip()` to also accept multi-line sub-agent output where `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` appears as the final line after a newline, not just as the sole content.
- Add focused unit tests for `sessions-send-tokens.ts` covering exact, whitespace-padded, multi-line, and negative cases.
- Add an e2e regression test for the multi-line announce-skip scenario.

Closes #74071

## Problem

Sub-agents that produce a DM summary block followed by `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` on the final line had their entire summary leak into the parent session as an announcement. The strict equality check `(text ?? "").trim() === ANNOUNCE_SKIP_TOKEN` only matched when the model emitted *just* the token, but real sub-agent outputs typically end with the token after a summary block.

## Fix

`isAnnounceSkip()` now checks two conditions:
1. **Exact match** (existing): trimmed text equals the token
2. **Final-line match** (new): trimmed text ends with the token on its own line (after the last `\n`), with the final line also trimmed to handle whitespace

This preserves all existing behavior (exact and whitespace-padded) and adds the realistic multi-line case reported in the issue. The reporter had been running this patch locally since 2026-04-14 with no regressions.

## Test plan

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tokens.test.ts` — 16 new focused unit tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` — 9 existing tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts` — 3 existing tests (all pass)
- `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` — 15 existing tests (all pass)

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: sub-agent output ending with a final-line `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` should suppress completion announcement delivery, while `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` followed by more text should not be treated as a silent sentinel.
Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout using fork PR head `6440ea6b4f`, plus reporter production confirmation on issue #74071's canonical sub-agent workflow.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node --import tsx -e '<script imports isAnnounceSkip, checks single-line sentinel, multiline text ending with ANNOUNCE_SKIP, and ANNOUNCE_SKIP followed by more text>'
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "branch": "fork/fix/announce-skip-multiline-74071",
  "head": "6440ea6b4f",
  "command": "node --import tsx isAnnounceSkip proof",
  "cases": [
    {
      "name": "single-line sentinel",
      "lineCount": 1,
      "result": true
    },
    {
      "name": "multiline final-line sentinel",
      "lineCount": 3,
      "result": true
    },
    {
      "name": "sentinel not final",
      "lineCount": 2,
      "result": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix: a final-line `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` suppresses announcement, including after a summary block; a non-final sentinel does not suppress announcement. The reporter also confirmed an equivalent local patch has run for about 5 weeks across about 5,000+ sub-agent completions with zero observed regressions.
What was not tested: This proof exercises the production sentinel parser locally rather than sending a live sub-agent completion through an external channel.

## Notes

- `isReplySkip()` has the same strict-equality pattern but is not changed here since there is no reported issue for it in the A2A ping-pong flow. It could receive the same treatment in a follow-up if needed.
- Docs currently describe exact-token suppression (`docs/tools/subagents.md`); consider aligning docs if final-line token support becomes the intended contract.
