target.title: fix(approval): distinguish policy vs non-persistable reason when Allow Always unavailable
target.body:
Fixes #97069.

## What Problem This Solves

When a command includes shell redirection (e.g. `openclaw --version 2>&1`), Allow Always is correctly hidden because one-shot commands can't be safely persisted. But all nine approval prompt renderers (reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, and gateway API) incorrectly blame the effective approval policy—even when the effective policy is `ask=on-miss`. Users waste time misdiagnosing their approval policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is that `resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` returns the same `["allow-once", "deny"]` for both `ask=always` (policy) and one-shot persistence (non-persistable command). Downstream renderers can't tell the difference.

Rather than introducing a new typed protocol field (`allowAlwaysUnavailableReason`) — which #97081 attempted across 65 files — we thread the existing `ask` field (already present in `ExecApprovalRequestPayload`, `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`, `PendingApprovalView`, Control UI request state, and the gateway/node host pipeline) through the approval-pending data pipeline so all renderers can branch on it.

The fix is at the renderer layer, not the policy decision layer. Approval policy logic is unchanged.

## Root Cause

`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts:1824` — `resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` collapses both reasons (ask=always policy and one-shot persistence) into a single return value. Nine renderers check `!allowedDecisions.includes("allow-always")` and unconditionally emit the policy message.

Introduced by: gumadeiras `ba735d015809` (generic unavailable copy)
Made visible by: jesse-merhi `c9707ab635b9` (one-shot persistence for shell-redirected commands)
Confidence: clear

## User Impact

Users with `ask=on-miss` (or any non-always policy) who run commands with shell redirection will now see:

> Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

Instead of the misleading:

> The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.

Users with `ask=always` see the same policy message as before.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Approval prompt text blames policy when missing Allow Always is actually caused by one-shot/non-persistable command safety.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22.11.0, branch `fix/exec-approval-prompt-text-97069`, base commit `origin/main`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

**Reply renderer** (the function that builds gateway-to-channel approval prompts):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload } from './src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts';

console.log('=== ask=always ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({
  approvalId: 't1', approvalSlug: 's1',
  ask: 'always', allowedDecisions: ['allow-once', 'deny'],
  command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', host: 'gateway',
}).text);

console.log('=== ask=on-miss ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({
  approvalId: 't2', approvalSlug: 's2',
  ask: 'on-miss', allowedDecisions: ['allow-once', 'deny'],
  command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', host: 'gateway',
}).text);
"
```

**Forwarder renderer** (real `ExecApprovalRequest` objects through the channel-forwarding path):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildExecApprovalRequestMessage } from './src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts';

var now = Date.now();
var req = {
  id: 'exec-req-1', createdAtMs: now, expiresAtMs: now + 300000,
  request: { command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', cwd: '/home/user/project',
    host: 'gateway', agentId: 'main', security: 'allowlist' },
};

console.log('=== ask=always + allow-always excluded ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalRequestMessage(
  { ...req, request: { ...req.request, ask: 'always' } }
));

console.log('=== ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalRequestMessage(
  { ...req, request: { ...req.request, ask: 'on-miss', unavailableDecisions: ['allow-always'] } }
));
"
```

**Evidence after fix** — real production renderer output:

**Reply renderer**:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "..."

=== ask=always ===
The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.

=== ask=on-miss (one-shot) ===
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).
```

**Forwarder** (real `ExecApprovalRequest` objects — same shape as the gateway production path):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "..."

=== ask=always + allow-always excluded ===
🔒 Exec approval required
...
Allow Always is unavailable because the effective policy requires approval every time.

=== ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===
🔒 Exec approval required
...
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).
```

**Telegram approval paths** (same renderer called by `buildTelegramExecApprovalPendingPayload` and `approval-handler.runtime.ts`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import ... from './src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts'; ..."

=== Telegram: ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

=== Telegram: ask=always + allow-always excluded ===
The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.
```

| `ask` input | Message shown |
|---|---|
| `"always"` | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (unchanged) |
| `"on-miss"` (one-shot) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" (fixed) |
| `"off"` (full-auto with shell redirect) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" (fixed) |
| absent / null (plugin, legacy) | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (safe default) |

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts \
    src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts \
    ui/src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts
# all passed (with fix in commit 700f47c for approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts — see below)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All nine approval prompt renderers now show the appropriate message. Policy → policy text, one-shot → non-persistable text, absent ask → policy (safe default). Production pipeline (gateway + node hosts → ExecToolDetails → embedded handler) threads `ask` through. The node path uses `approvalDecisionAsk` (`maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)`) — keeping the reasoning consistent with `allowedDecisions` computation. Telegram native and forwarding paths pass `ask` through `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`. Gateway API error path uses the same `isPolicyAlways` heuristic.

Additional CI guard checks pass locally: `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke` (dts emit), `pnpm ui:i18n:check` (all locales clean).

**End-to-end Telegram pipeline proof**: The terminal renderer output is byte-identical to what the Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` endpoint receives. The pipeline has three layers with zero text transformations:

1. `buildPendingPayload()` (`approval-handler.runtime.ts:75`) → `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({ask, ...})` → returns `{ text, buttons }`
2. `deliverPending()` (`approval-handler.runtime.ts:162`) → `sendMessage(chatId, pendingPayload.text, {...})` — `pendingPayload.text` IS the Layer 1 result, passed verbatim
3. `sendMessageTelegram()` (`send.ts`) → calls Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` — text parameter passed without modification

No escaping, no MarkdownV2 transformation, no string manipulation occurs between layers. Therefore the terminal output above is the exact text Telegram displays.

**Test fix (commit 700f47c)**: The `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts` test "shows non-persistable reason in reaction prompts" initially used `allowedDecisions: ["allow-once", "deny"]` in the request payload. However, `buildPendingApprovalView()` → `resolveExecApprovalRequestAllowedDecisions()` computes decisions from `ask` + `unavailableDecisions` — it does **not** read `allowedDecisions` from the request. The field was silently ignored, `allow-always` was never excluded, and the test couldn't trigger the non-persistable message path. Fixed by changing to `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]`, which correctly feeds into `resolveExecApprovalRequestAllowedDecisions()`. The other two new tests (reply + forwarder) call `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload()` directly with `allowedDecisions` in the payload params, not the request — that path uses the field correctly via `resolveAllowedDecisions()`.

## Regression Test Plan

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts \
    src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts \
    ui/src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts
# all pass
```

New test cases added:
- `exec-approval-reply.test.ts`: "shows non-persistable reason when allow-always is excluded for non-policy reasons"
- `exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts`: "shows non-persistable reason when allow-always excluded for non-policy reasons"
- `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts`: "shows non-persistable reason in reaction prompts when allow-always excluded for one-shot"

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts`: +5/−1 — branch on `params.ask` in reply renderer
- `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`: +5/−1 — branch on `request.request.ask` in forwarder
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`: +6/−1 — accept `ask` in agent-facing pending message
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-types.ts`: +1 — add `ask` to `ExecToolDetails` approval-pending
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`: +3 — thread `ask` through `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult`
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts`: +1 — pass `hostAsk` to pending tool result
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts`: +2 — pass `approvalDecisionAsk` to pending result and request registration (not raw `hostAsk` — matches the `maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)` value used to compute `allowedDecisions`)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`: +3 — read and forward `ask` from details
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`: +7/−1 — branch on `ask` in reaction manual instruction, with `approvalKind === "exec"` discriminator guard for `PendingApprovalView` union type
- `extensions/telegram/src/exec-approval-forwarding.ts`: +1 — pass `params.request.request.ask` to reply payload
- `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`: +1 — pass `params.view.ask` (exec only) to reply payload
- `src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approval.ts`: +10/−7 — distinguish policy vs non-persistable in validateDecision error message
- `ui/src/ui/views/exec-approval.ts`: +11/−3 — use `allowAlwaysNonPersistable` i18n key for non-policy
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`: +2 — new `allowAlwaysNonPersistable` key
- `ui/src/i18n/`: sync-generated fallback keys for all other locales
- 3 test files: +54 new tests covering one-shot render path

---

**Update (2026-06-30)**: Rebased onto latest main and fixed `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/raw-copy-baseline.json` baseline drift (upstream PR #92654 added "Cancel reply" strings to `chat.ts` but forgot to sync the baseline — not a bug in this PR). All CI checks now pass. No source changes were needed beyond the baseline sync.

target.title: fix(infra): add NaN guard for date parse in session cost usage
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: In `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts`, the `loadSessionLogs()` function iterates over session transcript messages and parses their timestamps for use in session log responses. When `parsed.timestamp` exists as a string, the code calls `new Date(parsed.timestamp).getTime()` to convert it to a numeric Unix-epoch-milliseconds value. However, there is no `Number.isNaN()` guard on the parse result. If the timestamp string is unparseable, `new Date()` returns an invalid Date and `.getTime()` returns `NaN`. This NaN silently propagates into downstream log entries and through the gateway's `sessions.usage.logs` RPC response boundary.

**Solution**: Add a `Number.isNaN()` guard immediately after `new Date(parsed.timestamp).getTime()` with a fallback to `0` (Unix epoch), matching the default value. The existing `parseTimestamp` helper in the same module (line 867) already uses `Number.isNaN(parsed.valueOf())` for safe timestamp parsing, so this applies the same established pattern.

**What changed**: `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` — the `loadSessionLogs()` timestamp parse path (line 2733-2735). Changed from unbraced single-line `if` to braced multi-line guard per repo `curly` lint rule:

```typescript
timestamp = new Date(parsed.timestamp).getTime();
if (Number.isNaN(timestamp)) {
  timestamp = 0;
}
```

**What did NOT change**: The numeric timestamp path, the default zero initialization, all downstream log formatting, the public API of `loadSessionLogs()`. All valid timestamps continue to parse identically.

Fixes #99413

## Linked context

- **Related PRs**: #94096, #93903, #89448
- **In scope**: `loadSessionLogs()` top-level transcript timestamp string parse path at line 2731-2735
- **Out of scope**: Other `new Date()` call sites without NaN guards — candidates for separate follow-up PRs

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: A session transcript message has a `timestamp` field that is a string but not a valid date parseable by `new Date()`. The code handles "string" and "number" cases but not the "string that fails to parse" boundary case.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unparseable timestamp strings in session transcript data no longer produce `NaN` in `loadSessionLogs()` output; they safely fall back to `0` (Unix epoch).
**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 LTSC 2019, Node.js v22.11.0, openclaw @ commit 367df9ec1e
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Ran inline Node.js parser simulation with 7 distinct timestamp input types (valid ISO, garbage text, empty string, numeric, undefined), plus dedicated regression test `defaults timestamp to 0 when a malformed timestamp string is unparseable` in `session-cost-usage.test.ts` exercising the real `loadSessionLogs()` function with JSONL transcript files containing malformed timestamp strings.
**After-fix evidence**: Before fix: garbage text and empty string both produce NaN. After fix: garbage text and empty string both produce 0. Valid timestamps produce identical values before and after. Regression test at `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` creates session transcript JSONL files with malformed timestamps, calls real `loadSessionLogs()`, and asserts `logs[0].timestamp === 0` for the malformed entry and `logs[1].timestamp > 0` for the valid entry.
**Observed result after the fix**: Three previously-NaN-producing inputs ("not-a-date", "", "!!garbage-input!!") correctly return 0 instead of NaN. Valid ISO-8601 timestamps continue to parse to correct numeric values. Numeric timestamps pass through unchanged. Missing timestamps (undefined) default to 0. NaN propagation demonstration: NaN + 100 = NaN, NaN - 50 = NaN, JSON.stringify(NaN) = null, confirming one bad timestamp poisons all downstream calculations without the guard.
**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end gateway `sessions.usage.logs` RPC response with deliberately corrupted session transcript data injected into a running OpenClaw gateway instance. This would require starting a gateway, manually editing transcript JSONL files to inject malformed timestamps, and calling the usage API endpoint. The guard logic has been verified through inline parser simulation (7 input cases) and a dedicated regression test exercising the real `loadSessionLogs()` function with malformed transcript fixtures.

## Tests and validation

Regression test added to `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: creates session transcript JSONL files with malformed timestamps, exercises real `loadSessionLogs()`, asserts malformed timestamps default to 0 while valid timestamps parse correctly.

```bash
npx vitest run src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t "defaults timestamp"
```

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — guard only activates on NaN; valid timestamps produce identical values
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — inline verification + dedicated regression test
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — PR body includes before/after comparison
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — N/A, zero breaking changes
- [x] Risk level: Low — defensive guard, fallback matches existing default, no API changes

target.title: fix: close FileHandles explicitly to prevent Node 26 GC crash
target.body:
## Summary

Node 26 promotes GC-finalized `FileHandle` from a deprecation warning to a hard `ERR_INVALID_STATE` error. Three locations in `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.3.0 skip explicit `handle.close()` when a stream `close` event fires (`handleClosedByStream` / `sourceClosedByStream` / `tempClosedByStream`), relying on the stream auto-close to release the fd. On Node 26 the `FileHandle` object still needs an explicit `.close()` call — otherwise the GC finalizer throws.

The leak affects the inbound-media path: `copyFileFallback` pipelines a bounded read stream (opened on `media/inbound/<uuid>.png`) into a temp write handle. After `pipeline()` resolves, both handles are skipped for close because their stream-close flags are `true`.

## Changes

### Patch: `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.3.0`

Removes the `if (!handleClosedByStream)` / `if (!sourceClosedByStream)` / `if (!tempClosedByStream)` guards before `handle.close()` calls in three functions:

1. **`writeStreamToTempSource`** (`file-store-boundary.js`) — always close `handle` after pipeline, in both success and catch paths
2. **`copyFileFallback`** (`root-impl.js`) — always close `source.handle` and `tempHandle` in `finally`, unconditionally
3. **`writeZipFileEntry`** (`archive.js`) — always close `tempHandle` after pipeline and in `finally`

Double-close is safe (all calls are wrapped in `.catch()`).

### Fix: `src/infra/gateway-lock.ts`

`acquireGatewayLock` opened a `FileHandle` with `fs.open(lockPath, "wx")` but if `handle.writeFile()` threw, the handle was never closed (no `finally` block). Fixed by moving `handle` to a block-scoped variable that is cleared on success and closed in the `catch` block on error.

### Tests: `src/infra/fs-safe.test.ts`

Added regression tests verifying that `copyIn` properly closes source `FileHandle`s, both on success and on `too-large` error.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual test: `copyIn` succeeds and file is readable
- [x] Manual test: `copyIn` with `maxBytes` rejects `too-large` and source is intact
- [ ] CI: `pnpm test` passes
- [ ] CI: `check-package-patches` guard passes with new allowlist entry

Fixes #99263

target.title: fix(hooks): flag hook event names that no core trigger emits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A hook's `HOOK.md` frontmatter declares which internal events it subscribes to (`metadata.openclaw.events`), but the loader accepts any string: `registerInternalHook(eventKey)` registers arbitrary keys, and only an *empty* events array produces a warning (`src/hooks/loader.ts`). Since core is the only emitter of internal hook events, a misspelled name (`command:nwe`, `message:recieved`, `gateway:started`) loads "successfully" and then silently never fires — no loader warning, nothing in `openclaw hooks list`/`info`, no way to tell a dead subscription from a hook that simply hasn't triggered yet. Debugging "my hook never runs" today means reading core source to discover the valid key set.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core-emitted key set is small, closed, and already documented (the events table in `docs/automation/hooks.md`): core trigger sites emit exactly 14 `family:action` keys, and hooks may also subscribe to a bare family (`command`, `session`, `agent`, `gateway`, `message`) to receive every action. Plugins *can* emit additional keys through the deprecated `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime` barrel (all bundled plugins emit only known keys — Telegram/Slack/Signal/WhatsApp emit `message:received`/`message:sent`), so a name outside the core set is *almost always* a typo — the diagnostics say so honestly ("not emitted by OpenClaw core — likely a typo; unless a plugin emits it, the hook never fires") and stay strictly advisory.

This change makes that set checkable:

- `KNOWN_INTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_KEYS` + `isKnownInternalHookEventKey` in `src/hooks/internal-hook-types.ts` (colocated with the `InternalHookEventType` union; the list mirrors the docs table and each entry was verified against its `createInternalHookEvent` call site, including the dynamic ones — `performGatewaySessionReset` emits `"new" | "reset"`, reset-command hooks emit `ResetCommandAction = "new" | "reset"`).
- The loader warns when a hook declares events outside the core-emitted set, naming the hook, the keys, and the docs URL — for both directory-discovered `HOOK.md` hooks and the legacy `hooks.internal.handlers` config shape. The hook is **still registered unchanged** — validation is advisory, zero behavior change, so plugin-emitted custom events and version skew degrade to today's behavior plus a warning rather than a refusal to load.
- `HookStatusEntry` gains `unknownEvents`; `openclaw hooks info <name>` renders a `⚠ Event not emitted by core (likely typo): …` line and the JSON report includes the field, so the diagnosis is visible after load time too.
- `docs/automation/hooks.md` documents the behavior next to the events table.

## User Impact

Hook authors find out about dead subscriptions immediately (gateway log at load) and on demand (`openclaw hooks info`), instead of shipping a hook that silently does nothing. Existing hooks with valid events see no change; hooks with typos keep loading exactly as before but are no longer silent about it.

## Evidence

HEAD: `f9b756725354debd4aa64cc62b36e411245b8e00` (base upstream/main `df350e6720`)

Real behavior proof (no mocks — a real `HOOK.md` declaring `["command:nwe", "command:new"]` loaded through the production `loadInternalHooks`, then rendered by the production status builder and CLI; captured at `607ca0ff76` — the one commit since, `f9b75672`, only adds the same advisory to the legacy `hooks.internal.handlers` path and does not touch the surfaces proven here):

```
=== 1. production loadInternalHooks over a real HOOK.md (watch the warning) ===
[hooks:loader] Hook 'typo-hook' subscribes to event command:nwe not emitted by OpenClaw core — likely a typo; unless a plugin emits it, the hook never fires. Known events: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/hooks
loaded hooks: 1; registered keys: command:nwe, command:new

=== 2. production hooks status report ===
hook=typo-hook events=[command:nwe, command:new] unknownEvents=[command:nwe]

=== 3. production `openclaw hooks info` rendering ===
  Events: command:nwe, command:new
  ⚠ Event not emitted by core (likely typo): command:nwe
```

Focused tests (all green locally):

- `src/hooks/internal-hook-types.test.ts` (new) — accept matrix for all 14 keys + 5 bare families; reject matrix for typos, bare actions, unknown families, case mismatches
- `src/hooks/loader.test.ts` — typo'd key still registers (advisory) and the valid subscription keeps firing; legacy config handlers get the same advisory treatment
- `src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts` — `hooks info` renders the ⚠ line
- `src/commands/onboard-hooks.test.ts` — fixture updated for the new required field
- `pnpm tsgo:core` + `pnpm tsgo:core:test` clean

External structured review: Codex (GPT-5.5), 5 rounds — flagged docs wording (bare-family subscriptions), an overclaim in this body ("plugins cannot emit new keys" vs. the deprecated `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime` re-export → diagnostics reworded to "not emitted by core / likely a typo"), and a missed sibling seam (the legacy `hooks.internal.handlers` path registered events without the advisory check → covered); final pass clean.

Known limits / Non-scope: advisory only — no fail-closed loading, no doctor check (the hooks CLI is the existing diagnostic surface), no change to the separate plugin-SDK hook API, no fuzzy matching/normalization of event names; no attempt to track plugin-emitted custom keys. New core trigger sites must add their key to the list + docs table (called out in a code comment at the list).

---

🤖 AI-assisted (Claude Fable 5 + Codex GPT-5.5 review loop). Prompt lineage: translate agentic-coding-tool hook-validation patterns (Claude Code hook-matcher fixes) into OpenClaw's internal hook loader; implementation, tests, review rounds, and the real-behavior proof were run locally as shown above.

target.title: fix(subagents): fail closed on thread binding without routable delivery origin
target.body:
## Summary
This PR enforces a fail-closed pattern when spawning a persistent thread-bound session subagent that fails to obtain a routable delivery origin during setup.

### Problems Solved
If a thread-bound session subagent (e.g. spawned via `sessions_spawn` with `spawnMode === "session"`) completes target binding successfully but without a routable `deliveryOrigin` (due to hook timeouts or channel anomalies), the provisional session is left alive, consuming context space and model API cycles, but remains unreachable for subsequent delivery or command routing.

### Changes
* Under `spawnMode === "session"`, if `hasBoundThreadDeliveryOrigin` yields `false` from `hasRoutableDeliveryOrigin(bindResult.deliveryOrigin)` but setup succeeds, the provisional child session is deleted immediately (`sessions.delete`).
* An explicit error is returned preventing the session state from drifting into an unrouted "zombie" state.

target.title: fix(subagents): sanitize subagent formatting and prevent internal content leakage
target.body:
## Summary
This PR adds output sanitation to subagent completion formatting to prevent internal system delimiters, untrusted content markers, and raw wrapper payloads from leaking into user channels.

### Problems Solved
1. **Internal Delimiter Leakage**: Delimiters like `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>`, `<<<BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_CHILD_RESULT>>>`, and security notice templates could leak directly to chats when a subagent fails or completes with unhandled output.
2. **Raw JSON Payload Leakage**: Raw JSON properties returned from CLI tools (like web_fetch results) were occasionally exposed, confusing messaging clients.
3. **Explicit Empty States**: Normalizes empty subagent runs to an explicit `(no output)` status block rather than failing format resolution or falling back to raw tool logs.

### Changes
* Introduced `isUnsafeSubagentDeliverableText(text)` checking for raw JSON shapes, security notice headers, and internal wrapper tags.
* Added sanitize check inside `selectSubagentOutputText` (output capture) and `resolveTextCompletionDirectFallback` (delivery).
* Added explicit fallbacks for empty event.result formatting in `formatChildResultData`.

target.title: fix(codex): key turn-abort detection on structural markers not prose
target.body:
## Summary

- Codex app-server abort detection now keys on the stable `<turn_aborted>` structural markers instead of byte-matching crate-internal guidance prose.
- Removes a latent upstream-coupling break: a reworded Codex guidance sentence no longer silently misclassifies aborted turns.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #99268 (the prose-coupling half). Deliberately does NOT auto-close: the structured-status classification path noted in review is a separate follow-up.

`isCodexTurnAbortMarkerNotification` classified interrupted turns by comparing the wrapped marker body strictly (`===`) against two full-sentence string literals (`CODEX_INTERRUPTED_USER_GUIDANCE` / `CODEX_INTERRUPTED_DEVELOPER_GUIDANCE`). Those sentences are declared `pub(crate) const` in `codex-rs/core/src/context/turn_aborted.rs` (verified against the pinned `@openai/codex` `0.142.4`) — crate-internal, not protocol surface. Any upstream reword or punctuation change would silently stop the equality match, misclassifying aborted turns with no error or log. This is the same failure class behind repeated abort/terminal-classification fix churn in this harness.

The `<turn_aborted>` tags in the same upstream file are the coarser, durable signal. This change keys detection on those markers alone (a non-empty body wrapped in the tags) and drops the guidance-sentence equality. The existing current-prompt echo guard still prevents false positives from the user prompt being echoed through raw response events.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts` — 29 passed (6 new, covering canonical guidance, a reworded body, developer role, missing markers, empty body, and prompt-echo guard).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts` — 66 passed (existing abort/interrupt integration coverage unchanged).
- Did NOT change: the `<turn_aborted>` marker constants themselves, nor the current-prompt echo suppression logic.

target.title: feat: add slash command picker in chat composer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has many slash commands, but the chat composer did not provide an in-context way to discover, filter, and select them. Users had to know command names ahead of time, and invalid slash input could still reach send-time flows without clear composer-side handling.

This PR adds a slash command picker that opens when the user types `/`, supports category switching between commands and skills, filters results as the user types, and validates slash-style input before sending.

## Evidence

- Added focused Swift coverage for slash command picker state and send-time validation in `OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Added iOS gateway coverage in `apps/ios/Tests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests.swift` for the command catalog transport surface.
- Captured UI screenshots from the implemented picker states:
  - Full picker: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-all.png?raw=true
  - Commands tab: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-commands.png?raw=true
  - Skills tab: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-skills.png?raw=true

## Design Philosophy

Since OpenClaw has many slash commands, the picker appears directly from the chat composer instead of requiring a separate reference page or memorized command names. The UI keeps the command name, description, and category visible so users can choose quickly without losing message context.

### Key Features

- **Instant trigger**: Type `/` to open the floating picker
- **Category tabs**: Switch between Commands and Skills views
- **Live filtering**: Start typing to filter the list in real time
- **Rich metadata**: Each item shows its name, description, and category badge
- **Send-time validation**: Invalid slash input is intercepted before sending

### Screenshots

**Full picker - all commands and skills**
![Slash Panel All](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-all.png?raw=true)

**Filtered to commands only**
![Slash Panel Commands](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-commands.png?raw=true)

**Filtered to skills only**
![Slash Panel Skills](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-skills.png?raw=true)


## Follow-up Evidence for bb1dba00e6

- Fixed the catalog request to include the active agent context derived from `agent:<id>:...` session keys before calling `commands.list`.
- Softened client-side slash validation so uncataloged slash-prefixed text continues through `chat.send`; the Gateway remains the final parser/authorizer.
- Added focused coverage for non-default-agent catalog loading and uncataloged slash send-path behavior.
- Local verification:
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "slash command"` passed.
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "unknown leading slash"` passed.
  - `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' -only-testing:OpenClawTests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests` passed.
  - `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests --no-parallel` still has existing async timeout failures outside the slash-command tests; all slash-command tests in that run passed.

target.title: fix: strip conda env marker from host tool runs
target.body:
Closes #99424

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw-managed host subprocesses could inherit Conda's active/default environment selectors from the parent process. Stripping only `CONDA_PREFIX` is insufficient: current Conda source falls back to `CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV` when resolving `Context.default_prefix` without an active prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared host-exec security policy already strips `VIRTUAL_ENV`. This change adds both Conda selectors to the same blocked-override-only bucket, which also makes them blocked inherited keys:

- `CONDA_PREFIX`
- `CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV`

The policy remains narrow. It does not add a broad `CONDA_` prefix rule or change `PATH` handling. The generated macOS policy mirror and reported baseline are regenerated from the same canonical policy.

The `CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV` half was converged from closed competing PR #99440 after direct review of [Conda's current default-prefix resolution](https://github.com/conda/conda/blob/56a19243422cb08f3791f901048a4e0d089e6472/conda/base/context.py#L812-L828).

## User Impact

Launching OpenClaw from an activated Conda shell no longer passes either Conda target selector into managed host subprocesses. Unrelated inherited environment behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before: current main and shipped v2026.6.11 block `VIRTUAL_ENV` but neither Conda selector.
- Contributor live proof: a real Conda-activated Windows parent had `CONDA_PREFIX` set; an OpenClaw-sanitized child received no prefix, rejected a requested prefix override, and exited 0.
- Maintainer child-process proof on the improved head:

  ```json
  {"rejected":["CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV","CONDA_PREFIX"],"child":{"CONDA_PREFIX":null,"CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV":null,"OPENCLAW_CLI":"1"},"status":0}
  ```

- Focused tests:

  ```text
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.policy-parity.test.ts
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
  Tests       42 passed (42)

  node scripts/generate-host-env-security-policy-swift.mjs --check
  OK apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/HostEnvSecurityPolicy.generated.swift
  ```

- Fresh autoreview after the two-selector improvement: no accepted/actionable findings.

What was not tested: the maintainer machine has no local Conda installation. The contributor proof covers a real Conda parent; the maintainer proof covers the improved two-selector sanitizer and real child-process boundary.

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites: WhatsApp **979/979**, Discord **1810/1810**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base `6cb82eaab8` (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).

**Real gateway restart-replay proof** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`). Discord/Mattermost flip the identical mechanism.

**Why the WhatsApp half has no live repro.** The #97538 failure state cannot be reproduced on demand: the reporter's pending backlog accumulated over ~7 days of production WhatsApp traffic, and ClawSweeper's 2026-06-28 review of the issue likewise states no high-confidence live current-main reproduction exists. That half is validated at the exact layer where the defect lives:

- The queue-backed journal tests run against the **real SQLite `channel_ingress_events` queue** (temp state dir), not mocks — `fail()` tombstones, attempt counting, and dead-letter-at-cap are exercised on the production storage engine.
- The "stall" mode that drives the storm is simulated directly: a replay pass whose `process` neither completes nor releases (the exact signature of a wedged run) must still record the attempt — asserted as `attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter across passes.
- The restart boundary is what the persistence tests simulate by construction: a **fresh guard/journal instance against the same persisted namespace** is semantically identical to a process restart (empty in-memory state, same durable rows). A live restart exercises no additional code path in the changed surface.
- The channel-side wiring is a thin adapter (constants + logging callback) covered by the full WhatsApp suite (986 tests), and the healthy path is behaviorally unchanged: completed events never replay (as before), and the cap only engages after 5 failed attempts of the same event.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).

target.title: feat(cli): render claude CLI native thinking with /reasoning gating
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem.** The `claude-cli` (claude-stdio) backend emits native reasoning on its stream-json output
— `stream_event › content_block_delta › delta.thinking_delta` plus a final assistant snapshot with
`thinking` content blocks — but `main`'s CLI parser (`createCliJsonlStreamingParser` in
`src/agents/cli-output.ts`) has no thinking handling at all. CLI-backed agents never surface reasoning
on any surface, in any `/reasoning` mode. Related open feature requests: #68374, #97526.

**Why now.** This is the parse-and-gate half of that gap, sized to land cleanly on current `main`
(post-#98907, where the channel-side streamed-progress-lane render layer is already generic/shared
across channels). See "Relationship to #97565" below for why this is filed as a separate, narrower fix.

**Outcome.** CLI reasoning now rides the exact same privacy gate embedded-agent reasoning already
uses: `/reasoning off` → nothing on any surface; `stream` → live window preview only; `on` → a durable
final reasoning payload (plus the same "control-UI/SDK sees raw thinking always, gated client-side"
characteristic embedded already has — see the proof section). No existing behavior removed; this only
adds handling where main today silently drops the data.

**Out of scope.** The live channel-preview render UX (Discord/Telegram progress-message formatting)
already exists generically post-#98907 and is reused as-is, not touched. This PR does not add any new
UI surface — it only makes CLI-sourced reasoning reach the surfaces that already exist for embedded
reasoning.

**Success criteria.** A claude-cli-backed agent turn with tool calls streams/persists reasoning
identically (privacy-wise) to an embedded-agent turn, verified at each of the three `/reasoning` states.

**Reviewer focus.** (1) the per-Anthropic-message reset in `cli-output.ts` (a tool round-trip within one
CLI turn starts a fresh Anthropic message with content-block indices restarting at 0 — the tracker must
not let a prior message's index-0 thinking bleed into the new one); (2) the reuse (not reimplementation)
of the existing `requiresReasoningProgressOptIn` / `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` gates — no new gate
mechanism is introduced.

## Maintainer-ready classification

- **Fix classification:** feature-completion / correctness fix (adds missing parsing + wires it through
  an existing privacy gate; not a behavior change for any other provider).
- **Root cause:** `src/agents/cli-output.ts`'s CLI stream-json parser never implemented thinking-block
  handling, so `stream:"thinking"` was never emitted for CLI-backed turns, and the CLI dispatch layer
  (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.ts`) had a since-removed `claude-cli`-only heuristic
  (`shouldBridgeCliAssistantTextToReasoning`) that bridged *assistant text* as a reasoning proxy instead
  of real thinking data.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** reuses the identical mechanism embedded-agent reasoning uses
  end-to-end — same `stream:"thinking"` event shape (`{text, delta, isReasoningSnapshot}`), same
  `onReasoningStream({text, requiresReasoningProgressOptIn: true})` call contract consumed by Discord
  (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) and Telegram
  (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts`), same durable-payload shape
  (`{text, isReasoning: true}`) consumed by the universal drop gate in
  `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` (`reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`
  → drop). No new gate, no new payload shape, no channel-specific code added.
- **Patch-quality notes:** internal red-team (see Tests section) caught and fixed a real correctness bug
  (thinking-tracker state bleeding across an Anthropic-message boundary within one CLI turn) before this
  was filed — see the dedicated test "resets per-index thinking state on a new message within the same
  turn (tool round-trip)" in `cli-output.test.ts`.
- **Related-PR scan:** see below.

## Relationship to #97565

#97565 targets the same gap with broader scope, including a from-scratch channel render layer that
#98907 has since made largely generic. This PR is the narrower parse-and-gate half, reusing the
post-#98907 shared lane with no new render code. It independently reimplements #97565's replace-style
snapshot dedupe (credit to that PR for the approach) rather than copying it.

## Linked context

- Related: #68374 (expose claude-cli thinking as reasoning on `/v1/responses` + `/v1/chat/completions`) —
  this PR doesn't touch those HTTP surfaces (see proof section: the OpenAI-compat endpoint has no
  `stream:"thinking"` handler on either side of this diff), so it's a step toward #68374, not a close.
- Related: #97526 (claude-cli live-session stream thinking deltas to channel preview) — this PR delivers
  the underlying data (parse + privacy-gated delivery); the channel-preview UX #97526 asks for already
  exists generically post-#98907 and picks this data up for free once merged.
- Related (not a duplicate — see above): #97565.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed:** CLI-backed (claude-stdio) agent turns now surface native reasoning through the
standard thinking stream and durable-reasoning payload, gated by `/reasoning` off/stream/on exactly like
embedded-agent reasoning.

**Real environment tested:** An isolated gateway (`~/openclaw-p6-home`, port :19791, channels off, own
`OPENCLAW_HOME`) running an authenticated `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6` agent, with a tee shim on the
real `claude` binary (v2.1.187) capturing its actual stdout for a live turn (a 12-coin logic puzzle
prompt — chosen to reliably induce extended native thinking).

**Exact step / command:** Sent one live prompt through the isolated gateway's claude-cli live-session
path; the shim captured the CLI's raw stream-json output verbatim
(`~/openclaw-p6-home/cli-capture/1783049207-12111.stdout`, 119 KB, 251 raw JSONL lines). That capture
contains **92 real `thinking_delta` frames + 1 `signature_delta` + 2 snapshot `thinking` blocks** — genuine
model output, not synthetic fixture data.

**Evidence (boundary-injection method — disclosed, see "what was not tested" below):** Rather than
re-running a full gateway→Discord/Telegram round trip for the gating differential (channel bot auth +
live posting adds environment setup without adding proof strength once the gate code itself is read
directly — see next paragraph), the SAME 92 real captured frames were fed through the actual, unmodified
production parser (`createCliJsonlStreamingParser`) and the actual, unmodified dispatch bridge
(`runCliAgentWithLifecycle` / `createReasoningTextBridge`) via the project's existing vitest mocking
harness (same pattern as `agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts`), and the resulting window-stream events +
durable payload were passed through the REAL downstream gate predicates, copied verbatim with citations,
from the actual channel code:
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:631-632` —
  `reasoningDurableEnabled = reasoningLevel === "on"`, `reasoningWindowEnabled = reasoningLevel === "stream"`
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:1201` — window drop:
  `payload?.requiresReasoningProgressOptIn === true && !reasoningWindowEnabled`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts:~3533` — durable drop:
  `reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`

Neither gate is touched by this diff; they're the exact pre-existing gates embedded reasoning already
relies on.

**Observed result (tri-state, real frames end-to-end):**
```
rawCounts thinking_delta_frames=92 onThinkingDelta=92 onReasoningText=92 assistantChars=3700 reasoningChars=5637
state=off    window: 0 passed / 92 dropped | durable: DROPPED
state=stream window: 92 passed / 0 dropped | durable: DROPPED
state=on     window: 0 passed / 92 dropped | durable: PASSED (chars=5637)
```
This matches the intended parity table exactly: `off` = nothing on any gated surface; `stream` = live
window only; `on` = durable payload only (no live window in `on` mode, matching embedded's existing
`durable=on, window=stream` split).

**Control UI / SDK note (verified, not a gap):** `stream:"thinking"` also reaches Control UI/SDK websocket
subscribers via `src/gateway/server-chat.ts`, which relays the generic agent-event bus without its own
`reasoningLevel` check — this is true for embedded reasoning too (documented in
`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts`: "the thinking stream always reaches the bus... display surfaces
... gate presentation on their side"). Control UI applies its own **client-side** gate
(`ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts:2137`: `showReasoning = props.showThinking && reasoningLevel !== "off"`), which
CLI thinking inherits automatically since it uses the identical event shape. Verified by direct reading of
both files — not a P6-introduced surface, exact parity with embedded's existing multi-layer design.

**What was not tested:** a full live gateway conversation through an actual Discord/Telegram bot with
screen-captured render output at each `/reasoning` state (the earlier, now-superseded emit-always
iteration of this branch did do a live gateway run — see the superseded commit's history — but the
gating differential proven above is at the code layer these channel renderers consume from, which is
where the actual privacy decision is made).

**Proof limitations:** the tri-state proof above exercises the CLI-specific code (parser + bridge) for
real, and the shared downstream gate code by direct citation + harness application — it does not
independently re-verify the shared gate code's own correctness (that code is pre-existing, used
identically by embedded reasoning, and out of scope for this diff).

**Before evidence:** on `main` (no `stream:"thinking"` handling in `cli-output.ts`), feeding the same 92
real frames through the unmodified parser produces **zero** thinking events — confirmed in this branch's
predecessor iteration (see subproject `PROGRESS-20260703.md`, "Step 3 — LIVE before/after proof").

**Proof pack:**
- [tristate-proof.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/tristate-proof.txt) — the tri-state harness output above.
- [harness-tristate.test.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/harness-tristate.test.ts) — the harness that feeds the 92 real captured frames through the real parser + bridge + downstream gate predicates.

## Tests and validation

- `export PATH="/Users/marvin/node24/bin:$PATH"; node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts
  src/agents/cli-runner src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts` → **456 passed, 0 failed** (89 + 236 + 131 across 3
  vitest shards), including 8 new/changed tests covering: streaming + snapshot dedupe, tool-interleaved
  multi-block dedupe, the new message-boundary reset (tool round-trip), the reasoning→gate bridge, the
  silentExpected suppression, and the durable-payload-without-a-visible-answer case.
- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs` → clean build, no errors.
- Internal red-team review (independent pass over the complete diff) found and this PR fixes two real
  issues before filing: (1) the per-message thinking-tracker reset above; (2) the durable payload was
  previously dropped when a CLI turn produced thinking but no visible final answer — fixed by attaching
  the durable payload whenever reasoning text exists, independent of whether other payloads exist.


---

## Update — Round 2: queued follow-up reasoning gate

The durable `{isReasoning: true}` payload synthesized for claude-cli was delivered on the queued follow-up path (`resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads`) with no `/reasoning` gate at all, so a claude-cli queued follow-up with `/reasoning off` could leak internal reasoning to the channel as an ordinary visible message. `resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads` now takes a `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` flag and drops `isReasoning` payloads unless it's true; `followup-runner.ts` threads the real `opts.reasoningPayloadsEnabled` through at both call sites, from the same `GetReplyOptions` the direct dispatch path already reads. **This gives claude-cli follow-ups the exact same gate embedded follow-ups already use — no new mechanism, full parity.**

Proof: [`08-followup-proof.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/08-followup-proof.txt) — a queued-follow-up cell added to the tri-state harness, exercising the real `resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads` against the actual captured claude-cli reasoning payload (5637 chars): off/stream → resolver drops it, on → resolver keeps it eligible. CI: lint clean (3 shards), `check:test-types` clean, 414/414 tests across the 5 touched P6 suites.

**Scope note:** `routeReply`'s pre-existing suppression of `isReasoning` payloads on the origin-routing branch (`route-reply.ts:131`, `shouldSuppressReasoningPayload`) is unchanged by this PR and is shared with the embedded runner's own follow-up delivery — it is not introduced here. This PR closes the gate that decides whether a reasoning payload is even *eligible* for delivery on the queued follow-up path (parity with embedded); what `routeReply` itself does with an eligible payload once it reaches the origin-routing branch is pre-existing, unrelated behavior.

target.title: Fix/issue 98958 gateway lock fd leak
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98958: In `src/infra/gateway-lock.ts`, when `fs.open(lockPath, "wx")` succeeds but the subsequent `handle.writeFile()` fails (e.g. disk full / ENOSPC), the code throws `GatewayLockError` without closing the file handle or removing the partially-written lock file — leaking a file descriptor and leaving a stale lock artifact on disk.

## Root Cause

`acquireGatewayLock()` opens a lock file with `fs.open(lockPath, "wx")`, then writes the payload with `handle.writeFile()`. The outer `try-catch` only handled the `EEXIST` case (lock already held). Any other `writeFile` failure fell through to `throw new GatewayLockError(...)` without cleanup — the fd from `fs.open` was never closed and the partially-written lock file was never removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the payload-write block in a nested `try-catch` inside the existing `try` block. When `writeFile` fails:

1. Close the file handle (`await handle.close()`) to release the fd
2. Remove the lock file (`await fs.rm(lockPath, { force: true })`) to clean up the stale artifact

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
Fixes #99273.

## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` checked `params.api !== "openai-completions"` when it should have checked `params.api === "openai-completions"`. The inverted condition meant that explicitly setting `api: "openai-completions"` for the `openai` provider fell through to the default URL/provider check and returned `true` (use responses transport), overriding the user's configuration.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: `api: "openai-completions"` config is ignored for `openai/*` models.

**Real environment tested**: Node 22.19+, local OpenClaw checkout.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx -e "..."
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
=== shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport (fixed) ===
api                       | provider | baseUrl          | result | expected
(unset)                   | openai   | (default)          | true   | true     ✅
openai-completions        | openai   | (default)          | false  | false    ✅
openai-chatgpt-responses  | openai   | (default)          | true   | true     ✅
openai-completions        | openai   | custom URL         | false  | false    ✅
```

BEFORE fix: api=openai-completions returned true → FORCED responses → hang ❌
AFTER fix:  api=openai-completions returns false → uses completions → OK ✅

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  45 passed (45)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts
 (passed, exit 0)
```

**Observed result after fix**: The `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` function correctly returns `false` when `api: "openai-completions"` is set, preserving the user's configuration. Default behavior (no api set) is unchanged.

**What was not tested**: Live E2E with a real OpenAI endpoint in completions mode. The fix is verified at the transport normalization boundary which is the exact drop point for this regression.

## Root Cause

A single char bug in `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` (`extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts:462`): `!==` was used instead of `===` when checking for `"openai-completions"`. The condition was intended to short-circuit when the user explicitly requested completions mode, but the inverted operator caused completions to fall through to the default responses path.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
- **Co-Authored-By**: Already in commit message

target.title: fix: prevent doctor --fix from exiting 1 when shell completion install fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` completes every doctor check green, then throws `Error: Failed to install completion: EACCES: permission denied` and exits 1 when the shell rc file (e.g. ~/.bashrc) is read-only. This happens deterministically in sandboxed environments like NVIDIA NemoClaw where ~/.bashrc is root-owned mode 444 for security hardening.

Fixes #99237

## Why This Change Was Made

The `doctorShellCompletion()` function in `src/commands/doctor-completion.ts` calls `installCompletion()` to write shell completion blocks into the user's rc file. Both call sites (slow-pattern upgrade and new-install paths) could throw on EACCES, propagating an uncaught error that set the doctor exit code to 1.

Shell completion is an optional step — doctor already skips it in `--non-interactive` mode. The fix wraps both `installCompletion()` calls in try/catch and emits a `note()` with the profile path and a hint to run `openclaw completion install` against a writable rc file instead.

## Evidence

### Tests

```
✓ |commands| ../../src/commands/doctor-completion.test.ts (6 tests)
  ✓ shell completion health mapping > checks an explicit shell instead of the detected environment shell
  ✓ shell completion health mapping > reports slow dynamic shell completion with dry-run effects
  ✓ shell completion health mapping > reports missing completion cache with a dry-run cache effect
  ✓ shell completion health mapping > keeps healthy shell completion quiet
  ✓ doctorShellCompletion > does not throw when installCompletion fails with EACCES in the slow-pattern upgrade path
  ✓ doctorShellCompletion > does not throw when installCompletion fails with EACCES in the new-install path
```

### Before-fix vs After-fix

**Before**: With a read-only .zshrc, `doctor --fix` exits 1:
```
$ openclaw doctor --fix; echo "exit:$?"
...
Error: Failed to install completion: EACCES: permission denied, open '/sandbox/.bashrc'
exit:1
```

**After**: With the same read-only rc file, doctor completes with a warning note and exits 0:
```
◇  Shell completion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Shell completion not installed:                                   │
│  /home/user/.zshrc is not writable. Run                           │
│  `openclaw completion install` against a writable shell profile.  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

## Merge Risk

Low. The change only adds try/catch guards around optional shell completion writes. Core doctor checks (config, auth, skills, plugins, state integrity, security) are unaffected.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound suite runtime gateway JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts` used an unbounded
`await response.json()` on the gateway HTTP success path inside `fetchJson`.
A misbehaving or hostile gateway endpoint (or accidental huge payload) could
stream oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during `JSON.parse`
while QA Lab suite scenarios read config snapshots or apply config patches
over the local gateway transport.

Replacing the success read with `readProviderJsonResponse` caps JSON parsing at
16 MiB and emits labeled errors such as
`qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Lab's suite runtime gateway with the broader OpenClaw
response-limit campaign that already bounded sibling provider and channel
surfaces (Telegram plugin Bot API reads, Copilot token exchange, Google OAuth,
QA Lab Telegram live transport, etc.).

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts`:
  - imports `readProviderJsonResponse` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`
  - replaces `await response.json()` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-lab-suite-fetch-json")` in
    `fetchJson`

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts`:
  - adds regression test `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` using a
    real `Response` object and asserting the labeled cap error

* `scripts/proof-qa-lab-suite-gateway-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming gateway envelopes plus vitest
    regression hook

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized gateway JSON success bodies fail closed
instead of unbounded `JSON.parse` allocation on the QA Lab suite runtime
gateway path.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 15.3.1, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helper from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB gateway `{ payload: ... }` envelope from a local HTTP
   server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` with label `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json` → assert
   labeled parse cap.
3. Drive the same helper on a buffered >16 MiB envelope (post-fetch handoff shape).
4. Verify a normal config snapshot envelope still parses.
5. Negative control: unbounded `response.json()` on a 64×1 MiB injected stream
   consumes all chunks without canceling.
6. Bounded helper cancels early on the same injected stream.
7. Run qa-lab vitest regression via `fetchJson("http://127.0.0.1:43123/config")`.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:


Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation


Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.
